A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniBal and retain matching methods and central experiments. Inspection of all 15 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and material among the references, supports reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-time measurements, downstream benchmark scores, component ablations and convergence/generalization experiments in Section 5 and Tables 1–11.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds computational profiling, threshold sensitivity, alternative preprocessing, hardware and GPU-scaling results.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the ISF sampling/filtering rules, profiled-anchor partition search using computation and communication metrics, and memory-based adaptive recomputation. v2 Section 4.3 supplies operational details for measuring memory savings and testing recomputation configurations; it does not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: The training datasets, instruction-tuning/pretraining tasks and downstream benchmarks are retained, including InternVL-1.2M, LLaVA-665K and LCS-558K. The Qwen2-VL experiment applies alternative preprocessing to the existing InternVL data and model. Hardware, GPU-count and preprocessing variations change experimental settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The backend, data-grouping and model-partition comparator sets remain unchanged. v1's 'sorted' comparator becomes 'length-group' with the same described grouping procedure, although its scores change. Qwen2-VL supplies preprocessing for an added experiment, rather than an additional competing model. PipeDream/DreamPipe refers to the same cited work.

E3.justification: v2 adds threshold sweeps, Qwen2-VL preprocessing, A100/H100 and network-bandwidth comparisons, and scaling tests using 64–512 GPUs. It also changes the stated partition-candidate timing budget from 20 training iterations in v1 Section 4.2 to three steps in v2 Section 5.1. This establishes a reported protocol revision, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative investigation of imbalance across stages, devices and time in Section 3, Table 1 and Figure 2; batching-threshold sensitivity in Table 6; and preprocessing, hardware and scaling analyses in Tables 14–16. These substantially extend the questions examined. Existing component ablations and ISF convergence analyses remain, with v1 Figure 5 retained as v2 Figure 4.

E5.justification: v2 adds mean-plus/minus-standard-deviation profiling summaries and explicit standard deviations for input, execution-time and memory variability in Table 1 and Figure 2. These describe workload variability, rather than uncertainty across independent training runs. Neither version supplies seed-based confidence intervals or repeated-training uncertainty for the main results.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 in v1 is numerically retained as Table 2 in v2. However, the sorted/length-group padding ratio changes from 0.014 to 0.20 and its ViT/LLM Dist Ratios from 0.47/0.40 to 0.26/0.13; device-group's LLM ratio changes from 0.228 to 0.15. v2 also adds profiling, sensitivity and new-setting results, including 40.2 versus 21.0 GPU days with Qwen2-VL preprocessing and 2.48–2.76× speedups across 64–512 H100 GPUs. These additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same padding/distribution ratios, partition objective and computation/communication metrics after notation cleanup. Neither version adds formal guarantees or proofs. The new inter-stage/intra-stage terminology and worked profiling examples provide conceptual and empirical analysis rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit contribution list claiming to be the first to identify and address computational imbalance in large-scale VLM instruct-tuning, and emphasizes balance across inter-stage and intra-stage levels. The three-component contribution, approximately 1.8× headline speedup and broad generalizability claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly argues why ordinary LLM packing cannot stabilize both vision and language inputs. It also explains LLaVA-1.6's smaller acceleration through its small vision encoder and predominantly data-level imbalance. These extend applicability and mechanism discussion while retaining the central explanations involving heterogeneous computation, pipeline bubbles and worst-case memory requirements.

D1.justification: v2 expands brief memory-profiling guidance into a four-step measurement and feasibility-testing procedure. It discloses five profiling steps, search radius r ≤ 3, 10–15 candidate partitions, 1K ViT tokens per image, and data-balancing-only use with the LLaVA DeepSpeed backend. Added tables specify GPU and network configurations. The code link remains, but release wording changes from a future promise to the ambiguous 'are be released'.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kosec et al.'s Packing work and contrasts text packing with VLM requirements. It removes the specific EVA-CLIP-18B reference while retaining the broader EVA-CLIP citation and experiments. The explicit first-to-address claim sharpens novelty positioning, but the main distributed-training and VLM research context remains.

P1.justification: The paper undergoes extensive rewriting and restructuring: related-work subsections are merged, problem analysis is reorganized, contributions are listed explicitly, recomputation explanations expand, and convergence/generalization become separate subsections. Author information also changes. Editing introduces an unresolved 'Section ??' reference in Section 4.1.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from one column to two, redraws Figure 1, replaces v1 Figures 2–4 with new imbalance and pipeline illustrations, and retains the convergence figure under a new number. It merges the ISF pseudocode blocks, adds five tables, and rearranges existing displays and captions. A long reference URL visibly overlaps the adjacent column.

improvement.justification: v2 provides direct hardware and scaling evidence for portability claims already made in v1, tests batching thresholds, and makes memory optimization and partition search easier to reproduce. These strengthen support and usability without changing the central findings. Unexplained baseline-ratio revisions, a broken section reference and reference-layout overlap temper the gains, making the overall improvement limited.
